_meta.description: M1-d golden: the four auto-evaluation judge signatures (instruction = class __doc__, fields in declaration order). Upstream float -> :number and str -> :string on the Elixir side.

SemanticRecallPrecision.instruction: Compare a system's response to the ground truth to compute its recall and precision. If asked to reason, enumerate key ideas in each response, and whether they are present in the other response.

fields.name: question
fields.desc: ${question}

fields.name: ground_truth
fields.desc: ${ground_truth}

fields.name: system_response
fields.desc: ${system_response}

fields.name: recall
fields.desc: fraction (out of 1.0) of ground truth covered by the system response

fields.name: precision
fields.desc: fraction (out of 1.0) of system response covered by the ground truth

DecompositionalSemanticRecallPrecision.instruction: Compare a system's response to the ground truth to compute recall and precision of key ideas. You will first enumerate key ideas in each response, discuss their overlap, and then report recall and precision.

fields.name: question
fields.desc: ${question}

fields.name: ground_truth
fields.desc: ${ground_truth}

fields.name: system_response
fields.desc: ${system_response}

fields.name: ground_truth_key_ideas
fields.desc: enumeration of key ideas in the ground truth

fields.name: system_response_key_ideas
fields.desc: enumeration of key ideas in the system response

fields.name: discussion
fields.desc: discussion of the overlap between ground truth and system response

fields.name: recall
fields.desc: fraction (out of 1.0) of ground truth covered by the system response

fields.name: precision
fields.desc: fraction (out of 1.0) of system response covered by the ground truth

AnswerCompleteness.instruction: Estimate the completeness of a system's responses, against the ground truth. You will first enumerate key ideas in each response, discuss their overlap, and then report completeness.

fields.name: question
fields.desc: ${question}

fields.name: ground_truth
fields.desc: ${ground_truth}

fields.name: system_response
fields.desc: ${system_response}

fields.name: ground_truth_key_ideas
fields.desc: enumeration of key ideas in the ground truth

fields.name: system_response_key_ideas
fields.desc: enumeration of key ideas in the system response

fields.name: discussion
fields.desc: discussion of the overlap between ground truth and system response

fields.name: completeness
fields.desc: fraction (out of 1.0) of ground truth covered by the system response

AnswerGroundedness.instruction: Estimate the groundedness of a system's responses, against real retrieved documents written by people. You will first enumerate whatever non-trivial or check-worthy claims are made in the system response, and then discuss the extent to which some or all of them can be deduced from the retrieved context and basic commonsense.

fields.name: question
fields.desc: ${question}

fields.name: retrieved_context
fields.desc: ${retrieved_context}

fields.name: system_response
fields.desc: ${system_response}

fields.name: system_response_claims
fields.desc: enumeration of non-trivial or check-worthy claims in the system response

fields.name: discussion
fields.desc: discussion of how supported the claims are by the retrieved context

fields.name: groundedness
fields.desc: fraction (out of 1.0) of system response supported by the retrieved context
